subject.title: [Bug]: QQBot severely compresses tall images after remote URLs are downloaded and re-uploaded

question: Is the evidence sufficient to permit QQBot to forward public image URLs to QQ again, or must the fix preserve OpenClaw-controlled downloading and eliminate compression through a different request shape?
rationale: Direct URL forwarding may restore image quality but transfers fetch authority to QQ and cannot preserve OpenClaw's pinned-download guarantees, while the current experiment has not isolated whether URL forwarding is actually necessary.

options.title: Prove bytes direct-send first
options.body: Require the four-path live request matrix and use `file_data + srv_send_msg=true` without a follow-up message if it preserves image quality.

options.title: Approve guarded URL forwarding
options.body: Allow an explicit public-image URL path with strict scheme and destination policy, focused security tests, documentation, and live QQ proof.

options.title: Retain the hardened path
options.body: Keep URL materialization and accept current image limitations until QQ or another non-lossy upload contract is available.

recommendation.title: Prove bytes direct-send first
recommendation.body: Require the four-path live request matrix and use `file_data + srv_send_msg=true` without a follow-up message if it preserves image quality.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work owns the relevant direct-media SSRF boundary and provides the closest history for evaluating a safe restoration.
